text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Human Rt was rated "outperform" by Bank Austria-Investment on the strength of expected approvals from the U.S.'s Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
"We anticipate FDA approval on several of its processes and products in late 1997 or early 1998, which will considerably boost 1998 results," analyst Lance Owen said in a report.
"We expect Human to perform well in the medium-term as a result of increased exports and stable domestic sales, thus meriting our rating of Human shares as 'outperform'".

Bank Austria-Investment expects Human to boost its HAS consolidated net income to 916 million forints in 1997 and 1.362 billion in 1998 from 710 million in 1996, while its net sales are seen growing to 16.055 billion in 1997 and 19.785 billion in 1998 from 13.657 billion in 1996.
Owen said Human was currently going through a period of a growth, with the company diversifying into different product lines and regions.

"Our expectations for the company in the medium-term is to progressively shift emphasis to export markets, of which a significant portion will be targeted to the markets of U.S. and Canada," he added.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Human shares finished at 2,920 forints, up 120.
